newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NO RESPITE FOR VICTORIOUS AUXERRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO RESPITE FOR VICTORIOUS AUXERRE.

text.p: European Cup quarter-finalists Auxerre face a tough two weeks before the winter break in France, starting with a home league match against Bordeaux on Saturday.
"We have two big, terrible weeks," said coach Guy Roux on Thursday. "Bordeaux, Olympique Marseille twice, Strasbourg, all good teams."

Auxerre, much to Roux's annoyance, have three matches in six days. After Wednesday's 2-1 Champions' League win over Glasgow Rangers, they meet Bordeaux then Marseille away on Tuesday in the League Cup.
They are also away to Marseille in the first division the following weekend and at home to Strasbourg before the break.
"The advance match (Tuesday) is for television. We are not protected," Roux complained.

Roux, typically keeping his feet firmly on the ground, said the French champions' task was not to slip below their sixth place in the first division and regain the top five to ensure European competition again next season.
"We are in danger like (1995 champions) Nantes. We must try to overcome the danger and book a place in Europe," Roux said the day after Auxerre beat Rangers to win their Champions' League group.

When it was suggested to him it was an advantage to face Jean-Pierre Papin's in-form Bordeaux side right after the cup success, Roux said: "The only thing is that they are going to respect us and that's a disadvantage."

Roux said that contrary to the impression some people had of him, he very much wanted to win the European Cup. But he pointed out the strengths and experience of Auxerre's quarter-final rivals Borussia Dortmund.
He said they had much greater financial clout and a squad "with 18 or 19 internationals, including seven foreign internatonals. They have been Germany's top club for four years."
Roux also hit out at the tough domestic programme his side face in contrast with Borussia's between now and the March quarter-finals.
He said: "Borussia play on Saturday then have a break until mid-February. The have only four (league) matches before the quarter-finals in March. We must have about 15."

Auxerre, counting the Bordeaux game on Friday, have eight league matches before the quarter-finals, four before and four after France's winter break which starts on December 20 and ends on January 25.
Nigerian defender Taribo West will be back to strenghten a still injury-weakened side against Bordeaux after missing Wednesday's European Cup match through suspension.
Australian defender Ned Zelic, goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier, midfielders Sabri Lamouchi and Christian Henna and winger Bernard Diomede are all on the injury list.
But Roux said they should all make it to Auxerre's five-day training camp from December 27 to 31.
